rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass with a clear stepped/terraced gesture, and it is legible in all four views rather than collapsing into a single-view trick. The parcel response is acceptable: the mass sits within the green boundary and does not obviously ignore the site frame. The blue access edge is answered only moderately well; there is a noticeable ground-level notch/void and some entry articulation, but it is not yet fully convincing as a public threshold aligned to the verified frontage. Programmatically, this is plausible for neighborhood living because it combines a compact primary volume with a usable void and upper hierarchy. The stepped silhouette is coherent and not merely arbitrary stair-stepping, though it still edges toward a generic terraced block. Repair integrity is strong: the solid remains continuous and avoids visible illegal-looking collisions or fragmented overlaps across views. Overall the mass is viable, but it would benefit from a cleaner, more public ground anchor and slightly stronger access-side void logic.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part composition with a legible central void and upper bridge/connector can support a neighborhood threshold while keeping the mass compact.
Long horizontal spread, courtyard-like opening, and a more site-responsive roofline suggest a public ground response without relying on a pure box.
Interlocking volumes and voids under elevated mass can strengthen hierarchy and daylight/public space sequencing.
A simple low-rise pavilion with a small entry articulation can reinforce active frontage when the main mass stays calm.
